notes: Federal filings (ASIC, ATO) plus each state's and territory's payroll tax and workers' compensation. The standard income year ends 30 June.

items.name: ASIC Annual Review — Fee and Solvency Resolution
items.rule: Within 2 months after the annual review date (the anniversary of registration)
items.description: ASIC issues an annual statement on the review date; the company checks its details, pays the review fee and the directors pass a solvency resolution. Changes are notified within 28 days.
items.authority: Australian Securities and Investments Commission (ASIC), Corporations Act 2001

items.name: Financial Report Lodged with ASIC
items.rule: Within 4 months after financial year end (3 months for disclosing entities)
items.applies: Public companies, large proprietary companies and foreign-controlled small proprietary companies that are not exempt
items.description: The financial report, directors' report and auditor's report are lodged on Form 388.

items.name: Annual General Meeting
items.rule: Within 5 months after financial year end
items.description: Public companies hold an AGM at least once each calendar year.
items.authority: Australian Securities and Investments Commission (ASIC), Corporations Act 2001 s.250N

items.name: Foreign Company Annual Financial Statements (Form 405)
items.rule: At least once every calendar year, at intervals of no more than 15 months
items.description: The foreign company lodges its balance sheet, profit and loss statement and cash flow statement with ASIC.

items.name: Company Tax Return
items.rule: 28 February after the income year (15 January for large and medium taxpayers; up to 15 May through a registered tax agent)
items.applies: Companies with a 30 June year end
items.description: The company tax return with any balance of tax payable.

items.name: Company Tax Return (substituted accounting period)
items.rule: 15th day of the 7th month after the end of the income year
items.applies: Companies whose income year does not end on 30 June
items.description: Companies with ATO approval to use another year end lodge on the equivalent date.

items.name: Income Tax Return (individual, partnership or trust)
items.rule: 31 October (later through a registered tax agent)
items.description: Sole traders report business income in their individual return; partnerships and trusts lodge their own returns and the partners or beneficiaries report their shares.

items.name: Business Name Renewal
items.rule: Before the registration expires (every 1 or 3 years)
items.applies: Businesses trading under a registered business name
items.description: Renewed through ASIC; an unrenewed name is cancelled.

items.name: PAYG Income Tax Instalments
items.applies: Businesses the ATO has entered into the PAYG instalments system
items.description: Instalments towards the year's income tax, reported on the activity statement.

items.name: GST Registration
items.rule: Within 21 days of GST turnover reaching A$75,000
items.applies: Businesses not yet registered for GST
items.description: Registration is voluntary below the threshold.

items.name: Business Activity Statement (quarterly GST)
items.description: GST collected and credits claimed for the quarter, with payment.

items.name: Business Activity Statement (monthly GST)
items.applies: GST-registered businesses with turnover of A$20 million or more, or that chose monthly reporting
items.description: GST collected and credits claimed for the month, with payment.

items.name: Annual GST Return
items.rule: 31 October (or the income tax return due date when a tax return is required)
items.applies: Businesses voluntarily registered for GST that report annually
items.description: One GST return for the year ended 30 June.

items.name: PAYG Withholding from Wages
items.rule: Small withholders: 28 October, 28 February, 28 April and 28 July (medium withholders: 21st of each following month)
items.description: Tax withheld from wages is reported on the activity statement and paid to the ATO; each pay run is reported through Single Touch Payroll.

items.name: Single Touch Payroll Finalisation Declaration
items.description: Confirms each employee's year-end payroll figures so their income statements are tax ready.

items.name: Superannuation Guarantee Contributions (Payday Super)
items.rule: Within 7 business days of each payday (from 1 July 2026; earlier quarters were due 28 days after the quarter)
items.description: Super contributions must reach the employee's fund within 7 business days of paying wages; late contributions attract the superannuation guarantee charge.

items.name: Fringe Benefits Tax Return
items.rule: 21 May (25 June when lodged electronically through a tax agent), for the FBT year ended 31 March
items.description: Reports benefits such as cars, loans and entertainment provided to employees.

items.name: International Dealings Schedule and Transfer Pricing Documentation
items.rule: With the company tax return (15th day of the 7th month after year end for most foreign-owned companies)
items.applies: Companies with international related-party dealings over A$2 million
items.description: The schedule is lodged with the tax return; transfer pricing documentation must exist by the lodgment date to support a reasonably arguable position.

items.name: Register of Foreign Ownership of Australian Assets
items.rule: Within 30 days of acquiring or disposing of a registrable interest
items.applies: Foreign persons holding interests in Australian land, entities or businesses
items.description: Foreign investors register acquisitions and changes through Online services for foreign investors.

employerItems.name: New South Wales Payroll Tax Return and Payment (monthly)
employerItems.applies: Employers whose Australian wages are above the New South Wales payroll tax threshold
employerItems.description: Payroll tax is charged by the state or territory where the wages are paid; an employer registers once its total Australian wages pass the threshold.

employerItems.name: New South Wales Payroll Tax Annual Reconciliation
employerItems.applies: Employers registered for New South Wales payroll tax
employerItems.description: Reconciles the year's wages and payroll tax; takes the place of the June monthly return.

employerItems.name: New South Wales Workers' Compensation Insurance — Renewal and Wage Declaration
employerItems.rule: At each policy renewal: declare actual wages for the past year and estimated wages for the next
employerItems.applies: Employers with workers in New South Wales
employerItems.description: Cover is compulsory for employers; premiums are set from the declared wages.
